title: On the Alignment of Large Language Models with Global Human Opinion

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing LLMs' verbalized opinion distributions on the World Values Survey (WVS) against actual human survey distributions from 66 different countries using a Wasserstein distance-based alignment metric to see if models over-align with specific countries (e.g., the United States).

Evaluating how translating the prompt and survey questions into a target country's native language (Language Steering) affects the model's alignment with that specific country's human opinion distribution compared to English.

Measuring the alignment of LLM opinion distributions against historical human opinion data across different time periods (Waves 5, 6, and 7 of the WVS) to determine if models favor contemporary views over historical ones.

Comparing the LLMs' opinion distributions against the average survey responses of various global religious affiliations (e.g., Protestant, Roman Catholic, Orthodox, Jew, Muslim, Hindu, Buddhist) to identify alignment disparities.
